docs.title: Atlan Application SDK
docs.text: Application SDK is a Python library for developing applications on the Atlan Platform. It provides a comprehensive PaaS (Platform as a Service) system with tools and services to build, test, and manage applications.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Install atlan-application-sdk as a dependency in your project:

  • Using uv (recommended): 

    uv add atlan-application-sdk

  • Using pip: 

    pip install atlan-application-sdk

[!TIP] View sample apps built using Application SDK here

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
To begin developing with the Application SDK:

  1. Clone the repository
  2. Follow the setup instructions for your platform:

docs.title: Configuration Reference
docs.text:
The Application SDK reads configuration from environment variables at startup. Variables are grouped below by subsystem. The canonical source of truth is application_sdk/constants.py (import-time constants) and application_sdk/main.py (AppConfig runtime values).

Set variables in your shell environment or Docker ENV / Kubernetes ConfigMap / Secret resources. For local development, a .env file at the project root also works: see .env.example at the repo root for a ready-to-copy template.

docs.title: The .env file
docs.text:
Only run_dev_combined() reads ./.env, as its first step, and a variable already set in the environment wins over the file. Importing application_sdk reads no file, so a production process never loads one.

run_dev_combined() runs after the SDK is imported, and the settings in application_sdk/constants.py are read at import. So a .env value reaches the runtime settings (AppConfig: ports, Temporal connection, task queue) but not the import-time ones (log level, OpenTelemetry exporters, application name in log tags). To apply the file to those too, load it before Python starts:

uv run --env-file .env python run_dev.py

The log line Loaded <names> from ./.env after the SDK was imported lists the variables the file set late.

docs.title: How values are read
docs.text:
Every variable follows the same rules:

  • Unset or empty means the default. An unset Helm value renders as "", so an empty value is treated as not configured. This holds for string variables too (names, paths, URLs): ATLAN_APPLICATION_NAME= means default, not an empty name. Surrounding whitespace is ignored.
  • A malformed value means the default, with a warning. OTEL_BATCH_SIZE=abc or an inf timeout does not stop the process. It logs a warning naming the variable and the value, and uses the default. Values read at import time (most of this page) warn on stderr, because logging is not set up yet. Values read later warn through the SDK logger.
  • Booleans: true, 1, yes and on enable. false, 0, no and off disable. Matching is case-insensitive and ignores surrounding whitespace. Any other word warns and keeps the default.
  • Choices (for example ATLAN_OOM_RESTART_CHECK, ATLAN_DEPLOYMENT_ARTIFACT_DUAL_WRITE): an unrecognised word warns and keeps the default.
  • Durations (the ATLAN_OBSTORE_*_TIMEOUT variables): one or more number-and-unit terms such as 30s, 90s, 1h 30m or 1.5h. Units are ns, us, ms, s, m, h, d, w, M (months) and y, plus their long forms. A bare number has no unit and is rejected (it warns and keeps the default), except 0, which is accepted as zero, as the object-store client accepts it.

ATLAN_SQL_USE_SERVER_SIDE_CURSOR is the one exception: an explicitly empty value disables server-side cursors, as it always has.

This page covers runtime variables only. Variables starting E2E_ configure the test harness under application_sdk/testing/. CI sets them, and a deployed app never reads them. See Runtime vs test-harness variables.

docs.title: Application
docs.text: Variable Default Description ATLAN_APP_MODULE (required) App class to load: module.path:ClassName (e.g. app.app:MyExtractor). Startup fails without it. Set in your Dockerfile as ENV ATLAN_APP_MODULE=… or pass via --app CLI flag. ATLAN_APP_MODE combined Run mode: worker, handler, or combined. Determines which subsystems start; override via --mode CLI flag. v2-compat fallback: APPLICATION_MODE (deprecated; case-insensitive; LOCAL/WORKER/SERVER map to combined/worker/handler, and the v3 names are accepted as-is. An unrecognised value logs a warning and runs combined). ATLAN_APPLICATION_NAME default Application name. Used in object-store paths, logging, and workflow identification. The default fallback applies to those identity uses only — task-queue derivation treats the variable as genuinely unset (see Task-queue naming). Set it as the bare name, with no atlan- prefix; the SDK adds the prefix. ATLAN_DEPLOYMENT_NAME local Deployment name. Distinguishes dev / staging / prod deployments of the same app. As with ATLAN_APPLICATION_NAME, the local fallback is an identity default and does not apply to task-queue derivation. ATLAN_TENANT_ID default Tenant identifier for multi-tenant deployments. ATLAN_DOMAIN_NAME atlan.com Tenant domain name. ATLAN_TEMPORARY_PATH ./local/tmp/ Path for intermediate files during processing. APPLICATION_SDK_ENABLE_CLEANUP_INTERCEPTOR true End-of-run cleanup. Read once at worker start and pinned on each run, which keeps the value it started with on any pod. When false, the default on_complete() skips cleanup_files() and cleanup_storage(), and a worker that releases a closed run's app state keeps the local files that run's tasks tracked. The run's app-state slot is still released and its cached clients closed. ATLAN_CLEANUP_BASE_PATHS (empty) Comma-separated object-store prefixes cleaned up by cleanup_files(). Defaults to the workflow-scoped run path when unset. ATLAN_CONTRACT_GENERATED_DIR app/generated Directory for generated contract JSON (configmaps, manifest). In Docker (WORKDIR=/app) this resolves to /app/app/generated. ATLAN_FRONTEND_ASSETS_PATH app/generated/frontend/static Path to static frontend assets served by the handler.

docs.title: Release metadata
docs.text:
Two sources, baked first. build-and-publish-app.yaml writes app/atlan_build.json into the image (app_version, commit_sha, image, built_at); the SDK reads it at startup. Deployers (Local Marketplace into the Helm release, the SDR orchestrator into the container) may still stamp env vars. When both exist the file wins: it describes the image, the env var describes what a deployer thinks it deployed. Images built before this CI started baking the file have no file and fall back to the env vars, then empty. Exposed to consumers via the OTel target_info gauge (one row per pod). Leave empty for local development. See standards/release-flow.md#image-identity.

Variable Default Description ATLAN_APPLICATION_VERSION (empty) Version of the app release as Global Marketplace stores it (release tag for semver apps, sha7 for CD apps). Used only when the baked file is absent or has no app_version. ATLAN_COMMIT_SHA (empty) Git commit the image was built from. Used only when the baked file is absent or has no commit_sha. Deployers do not normally stamp this. ATLAN_BUILD_INFO_PATH app/atlan_build.json Override the baked-identity lookup for non-template layouts whose Dockerfile does not copy app/. When unset, the SDK also tries <parent of ATLAN_CONTRACT_GENERATED_DIR>/atlan_build.json. ATLAN_BUILD_ID (empty) Immutable image tag, stamped as an image ENV by the e2e build action. Takes precedence over the baked file's build_id; both are read by application_sdk.app.build_identity.build_identity(). Not set on released images, which carry the value in the file instead. ATLAN_RELEASE_ID (empty) Release UUID from Global Marketplace. Injected by the deployer. ATLAN_RELEASE_CHANNEL (empty) Release channel (all, beta, staging, specific). ATLAN_SDK_VERSION (empty) SDK version used to build this app image. ATLAN_APP_TYPE (empty) App type from Global Marketplace (e.g. connector, system). ATLAN_PUBLISHED_AT (empty) Release publication timestamp (ISO 8601). ATLAN_APP_ID (empty) Global Marketplace's id for this app — the card's installation_id. One per app and stable across releases and tenants, unlike ATLAN_RELEASE_ID. Not yet stamped by any deployment, so every reader must tolerate an empty value and send nothing rather than a substitute.

docs.title: Preflight results store
docs.text:
Where the injected preflight gate appends its verdict. The route is served by another repo — see standards/cross-repo-contracts.md before changing either value.

Variable Default Description ATLAN_PREFLIGHT_RESULTS_ENDPOINT http://system-workflows.system-workflows-app.svc.cluster.local:8000/continuous-preflight/check-results The whole write URL, path included — never composed from parts. Override to point at a stub off-cluster. ATLAN_PREFLIGHT_RESULTS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 30 Bound on that POST. Generous because the receiving app opens a Polaris catalog, may create the table and commits a Parquet file. Nothing waits on it.

docs.title: SQL clients
docs.text: Variable Default Description ATLAN_SQL_CLIENT_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 60 Bound on a SQL client's load(): building the connection string (including the STS AssumeRole for IAM-role auth) plus the first connect. Expiry raises SqlClientConnectTimeoutError. Also passed as connect_timeout to psycopg2, psycopg and MySQLdb, which have no connect timeout of their own, unless DB_CONFIG.connect_args or the URL already sets one. For IAM-role auth, the STS AssumeRole call's limits (5 s connect, 15 s read, 2 attempts) shrink to fit the time left, so a hung STS call frees its worker thread by the deadline too.

docs.title: Temporal / Workflow
docs.text: Variable Default Description ATLAN_TEMPORAL_HOST localhost:7233 Temporal server address (host:port). v2-compat fallback: if unset, the SDK constructs the address from ATLAN_WORKFLOW_HOST + ATLAN_WORKFLOW_PORT (deprecated; remove when all deployments set ATLAN_TEMPORAL_HOST). ATLAN_TEMPORAL_NAMESPACE default Temporal namespace. v2-compat fallback: ATLAN_WORKFLOW_NAMESPACE. ATLAN_TASK_QUEUE (derived) Temporal task queue name. Defaults to atlan-{ATLAN_APPLICATION_NAME}-{ATLAN_DEPLOYMENT_NAME} when both are set, or just the bare app name (no atlan- prefix) when only ATLAN_APPLICATION_NAME is set, or {ClassName}-queue (kebab-case) when neither is set. Setting this explicitly also changes the queue the served manifest advertises, so a worker on an overridden queue and the Automation Engine stay in step. The override is for local and CLI runs: do not pin it in a deployed app's deploy or pool env (contract/app.pkl or atlan.yaml) — the on-demand (-od) worker then polls the base queue and its retries hang (conformance rule K031). See Task-queue naming. APPLICATION_SDK_ENABLE_OUTPUT_INTERCEPTOR true Collect get_outputs() metrics and artifacts and merge them into the workflow result. Each activity carries its outputs back on its own result (metrics / artifacts on an Output, or a reserved _atlan_outputs key on a dict result, which the workflow strips from its own dict result), so they arrive whichever worker runs the activity. An activity returning anything else (e.g. None) cannot carry them: they are dropped with a warning. Set it on workflow and activity workers alike. ATLAN_TEMPORAL_PROMETHEUS_BIND_ADDRESS 127.0.0.1:9464 Bind address for the Temporal SDK Prometheus endpoint (~40 built-in metrics). Loopback-only by default — operators should not scrape this port directly; combined-mode FastAPI /metrics proxies it in-process. See Monitoring. APPLICATION_SDK_ENABLE_EVENT_INTERCEPTOR true Publish lifecycle events (workflow and activity start/end) through the event binding. Read once at worker start and pinned on each run the worker starts, so a run publishes (or not) according to the worker that started it. ATLAN_POOL_<POOL>_QUEUE (derived) Task queue for tasks declared with @task(pool="<pool>"). <POOL> is the pool name upper-cased with - replaced by _ (cold-tier reads ATLAN_POOL_COLD_TIER_QUEUE). Unset means <task queue>-<pool>, from ATLAN_TASK_QUEUE or the derived queue. ATLAN_WORKFLOW_MAX_TIMEOUT_HOURS (unset: no limit) Execution timeout, in hours, the handler sets on the workflows it starts. Unset, 0 or negative means no timeout (a negative value logs a warning). TEMPORAL_HOST localhost:7233 Read by load_execution_settings() into ExecutionSettings.host, with ATLAN_WORKFLOW_HOST + ATLAN_WORKFLOW_PORT as the fallback. The SDK's own worker and client do not use this field: they connect with ATLAN_TEMPORAL_HOST. Set that one. TEMPORAL_NAMESPACE default Read into ExecutionSettings.namespace. Not used by the SDK's worker or client, which read ATLAN_TEMPORAL_NAMESPACE. TEMPORAL_TASK_QUEUE application-sdk Read into ExecutionSettings.task_queue. Not used by the SDK's worker or client, which read ATLAN_TASK_QUEUE.

docs.title: Task-queue naming
docs.text:
The queue name has to be agreed on by two things that never talk to each other: the worker, which polls it, and the served manifest, whose resolved task_queue the Automation Engine writes into the DAG and submits work to. When they disagree nothing fails loudly — AE submits to one queue, the worker polls another, and the run sits unclaimed until its 24h heartbeat backstop.

There is now one derivation, application_sdk.common.task_queue.derive_task_queue, and the manifest route does not re-run it — it stamps the queue the handler was configured with, which is the same value the worker was started on. Two paths deriving the same answer is a convention; one path copying the other's answer is structural.

The rule itself:

ATLAN_APPLICATION_NAME ATLAN_DEPLOYMENT_NAME Queue dbt prod atlan-dbt-prod dbt (unset) dbt — bare, no prefix (unset) anything no queue name exists; the worker falls back to {ClassName}-queue for local dev, and the manifest stamps that same queue. With no app name available anywhere, the served manifest leaves the literal {app_name} token in place and logs at ERROR

Two consequences worth internalising when writing or rewriting an AE DAG outside the toolkit:

  • Pass the bare app name. derive_task_queue adds the atlan- prefix. Prefixing a value that is already prefixed produces atlan-atlan-dbt-production, a queue nothing polls.
  • Never invent a name for the unset case. atlan-default-prod reads as a legitimate queue and reproduces the original silent hang; a literal {app_name} in the DAG is greppable and diagnosable in one step. That is why ATLAN_APPLICATION_NAME's default fallback is scoped to identity uses and excluded here.

Do not pin ATLAN_TASK_QUEUE in a deployed app. The chart runs an on-demand variant of the worker with -od appended to ATLAN_DEPLOYMENT_NAME, so the derivation gives it its own queue, atlan-{app}-{deployment}-od. An explicit ATLAN_TASK_QUEUE in the contract's deploy or pool env (or in atlan.yaml) overrides the derivation for both variants, so the -od worker polls the base queue. When a worker pod is lost, the activity rerouter moves the retry to the -od queue, nothing polls it, and the run hangs until its workflow timeout. Conformance rule K031 flags the pin. Setting it for a local or CLI run (--task-queue) is fine.

Nodes that dispatch to a different app's queue (atlan-publish-{deployment_name} and friends) are legitimately not this app's queue: their {deployment_name} token is filled and the value is otherwise left alone.

docs.title: Worker Versioning
docs.text:
Used by the Temporal Worker Deployment controller (TWD). Leave empty unless your cluster uses versioned deployments.

Variable Default Description ATLAN_APP_BUILD_ID (empty) Build ID for worker versioning. Fallback: TEMPORAL_BUILD_ID. ATLAN_APP_DEPLOYMENT_NAME (empty) Worker Deployment name (<namespace>/<twd-name>). Fallback: TEMPORAL_DEPLOYMENT_NAME. TEMPORAL_DEFAULT_VERSIONING_BEHAVIOR PINNED Versioning behavior for workflows that declare none, when the worker registers as a Worker Deployment version. PINNED or AUTO_UPGRADE (case-insensitive); any other value logs a warning and uses PINNED.

docs.title: Task timeouts and progress
docs.text:
Process-wide defaults for @task timing, read once at startup. An explicit value on @task(...) always wins. See Tasks: process-wide timeout defaults.

Variable Default Description ATLAN_START_TO_CLOSE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 86400 (24 h) Default timeout_seconds: Temporal ends one activity attempt after this many seconds. ATLAN_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 60 Default heartbeat_timeout_seconds: Temporal retries the activity when no heartbeat arrives within this window. The framework heartbeats every 10 s. ATLAN_SCHEDULE_TO_CLOSE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (unset: unbounded) Default schedule_to_close_seconds: ceiling on a task's total time across every retry. 0 reads as unset; a negative value logs a warning and is ignored. ATLAN_PROGRESS_WATCHDOG warn Stall-watchdog mode: off, warn or enforce. off disables the watchdog and beats a per-task declaration. An unrecognised value logs a warning and uses warn. ATLAN_MAX_NO_PROGRESS_SECONDS 900 Default max_no_progress_seconds: how long an attempt may report no progress before the watchdog reports a gap. 0 or negative uses the default. ATLAN_RUN_LENGTH_SLA_SECONDS 86400 (24 h) How long a run may take before the run-length alert is raised. 0 disables it. See Tasks. ATLAN_SDR_<OP>_START_TO_CLOSE_SECONDS 300 Per-attempt timeout for one SDR handler activity. <OP> is AUTH (test_auth), PREFLIGHT (preflight_check) or METADATA (fetch_metadata). ATLAN_SDR_<OP>_SCHEDULE_TO_CLOSE_SECONDS 300 Total-time ceiling for the same SDR activity across retries. A value lower than the matching start-to-close timeout logs a warning, because Temporal rejects that pair.

docs.title: Worker Restart Supervisor
docs.text:
Bounds the restart supervisor that rebuilds the worker after a fatal poll error (e.g. a transient auth failure) instead of exiting. Defaults are sensible; override only to tune restart behavior.

Variable Default Description ATLAN_WORKER_MAX_CONSECUTIVE_RESTARTS 10 Consecutive worker-fatal failures tolerated before the supervisor gives up and re-raises, so a persistent misconfiguration still fails loud instead of hot-looping. The counter resets after a healthy run window. ATLAN_WORKER_RESTART_BACKOFF_CAP_SECONDS 30 Upper bound (seconds) for the full-jitter exponential backoff between worker restarts. The backoff is raced against shutdown so SIGTERM stays responsive. ATLAN_WORKER_HEALTHY_RUN_SECONDS 300 A worker that ran at least this long (seconds) before failing is treated as a fresh incident, resetting the consecutive-failure streak. ATLAN_WORKER_POLL_DIAGNOSTIC_INTERVAL_SECONDS 60 How often (seconds) to read Temporal core's live poller gauge and log a state transition, so a worker that is alive but claiming no work is visible in logs and in the /live / /ready probe details. Its readings also drive the two poll-loop /live checks below, so the time those take to trip scales with this interval. Set to 0 to disable (the zero-poller check then never trips, and the fatal check can never see a recovery). ATLAN_WORKER_ZERO_POLLER_READINGS_BEFORE_STALE 3 Consecutive definitive zero-poller readings before this worker stops emitting token_refresh health events. At the default 60s observer interval that is ~3 minutes of confirmed-parked polling. unknown / polling never accumulate toward this threshold. ATLAN_WORKER_LIVENESS_MAX_ZERO_POLLER_READINGS 5 Consecutive definitive zero-poller readings before the worker /live probe returns 503, so Kubernetes restarts a pod that is alive but polling nothing. About 5 minutes at the default observer interval. unknown / polling reset the count. Set to 0 to disable. ATLAN_WORKER_LIVENESS_FATAL_RECOVERY_SECONDS 600 Seconds a fatal poll error may go without a later polling reading before the worker /live probe returns 503. When the poller gauge cannot be read, no recovery is visible, so every fatal restarts the pod after this bound. Set to 0 to disable. ATLAN_WORKER_LIVENESS_MAX_IMPORT_WAIT_SECONDS 300 Seconds one thread may wait on the same module import lock before the worker /live probe returns 503. Temporal's deadlock interrupt (TMPRL1101) can land inside Python's import system and leave a thread waiting on an import forever; every later import of that module then hangs while the worker keeps polling, so activities fail by heartbeat timeout. A healthy import never waits this long. Set to 0 to disable. ATLAN_WORKER_FATAL_TEARDOWN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS graceful shutdown timeout + 60 Upper bound (seconds) on temporalio's own worker teardown after a fatal poll error. The supervisor regains control only when that teardown returns; if it has not returned within this bound the process exits with code 1 so the pod or container restart policy brings up a fresh worker. 0 or negative disables the bound. ATLAN_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS unset The pod's terminationGracePeriodSeconds. Kubernetes' Downward API cannot expose that field, so the chart sets this env var from the same value. When set, the drain (TEMPORAL_GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT), the post-drain deadline (ATLAN_POST_DRAIN_EXIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) and the Pushgateway shutdown bounds (ATLAN_PROMETHEUS_PUSHGATEWAY_HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, ATLAN_PROMETHEUS_PUSHGATEWAY_SHUTDOWN_DELETE_DELAY_SECONDS) default to values derived from it, and the event-loop stall bound (ATLAN_WORKER_LOOP_STALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) is capped so it still fires before SIGKILL. The drain comes first: in-flight activities are the one step that is not best-effort, and daprd stays up for the whole drain because the entrypoint stops it only after Python exits. The steps after the drain (post-drain deadline and daprd's stop) would ideally get min(120, grace/4) + min(30, grace/10). They never take that from a drain of up to TEMPORAL_GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT (or its 3600 s default): they get what the grace leaves beyond that drain, but never less than 10 s, and the drain gets the rest after ATLAN_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_DELAY_SECONDS. A 12 h grace keeps 120/10/35 s and drains for ~12 h. A 3660 s grace keeps the full 3600 s drain, and the Pushgateway hold shrinks into the 55 s left. A 30 s grace drains for 15 s. An explicit value for any single bound still wins. At startup the worker logs the effective budget, and logs a WARNING when explicit bounds add up to more than the grace. Unset, every bound keeps its fixed default. A grace too short to cover ATLAN_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_DELAY_SECONDS plus a 1 s post-drain deadline also keeps the defaults, with a warning. The WARNING about explicit bounds counts the daprd headroom too. ATLAN_WORKER_LOOP_STALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS derived Replaces the event-loop stall bound for a shutting-down worker. SIGTERM is handled on the event loop, so a loop stuck in a lock wait or an untimed blocking call never shuts down: Temporal's core keeps polling on its own threads and takes tasks the process cannot run until SIGKILL, and the kubelet no longer runs liveness probes on a terminating pod. The stall watchdog closes that gap and is armed only by the first SIGTERM or SIGINT; before shutdown a frozen loop is left to a liveness probe on the worker's /live, which runs on the same loop. It arms from a process-level signal handler, which the interpreter runs only when the main thread is back in Python bytecode. A loop already frozen in a lock wait (threading.Lock and the like) or in a blocking system call that Python retries after a signal (PEP 475: open, read, sleep, ...) is covered. A native call that keeps waiting inside C delays the arming until it returns, whether or not it released the GIL (a database driver's busy-wait, for example), and a native call that never returns (a driver or Rust/C mutex) never arms it, which leaves that freeze to SIGKILL. A freeze that starts after the signal is always covered. While the loop runs through the drain it keeps pushing the deadline back, and it is stopped when the drain ends and ATLAN_POST_DRAIN_EXIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS takes over. If the loop does not run for the bound, the process writes every thread's stack to stderr and exits with code 1 (the timer runs the bound plus one re-arm interval, min(bound/4, 15 s), so the loop has been silent for at least the bound, unless the SIGKILL cap below cut it short). Unset, the bound is 15 s past the longest heartbeat_timeout_seconds among the registered tasks (at least the 60 s default), so a stall during the drain never ends work Temporal still counts as alive. Tasks without a heartbeat timeout do not count: once the loop stops they are indistinguishable from a freeze, and Temporal reclaims them only at their start-to-close timeout; startup logs a WARNING naming each app task without a heartbeat timeout whose start-to-close timeout is longer than the bound. With ATLAN_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS declared the bound is also capped so the exit lands before SIGKILL with daprd's headroom left (a 30 s grace gives 22.4 s), and the drain's re-arms never push the exit later than that point after the signal, so a freeze that starts late in the drain still ends the process before SIGKILL. The derived drain timeout ends before that point, so the cap only ends a drain that overruns it (an activity still running after it was cancelled, for example); that exit has the same stack dump and code 1 even though the loop may still be running, so the loop first logs a WARNING ("Shutdown drain still running at the exit deadline") saying the dump that follows marks the deadline, not a stalled loop. The bound shows as loop_stall= in the startup Shutdown budget line, with a WARNING when longest heartbeat timeout < bound <= what still fires before SIGKILL does not hold because of an override or a task's own heartbeat timeout (the WARNING names the task). When only the SDK's default heartbeat timeout (ATLAN_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) is longer than a short grace allows, the same fact is logged at INFO, since no task is at fault. Set it to 0 to turn the watchdog off, for example when debugging a worker locally, where a breakpoint during shutdown would otherwise end the process. Applies when the app is started through the SDK's entry point (python -m application_sdk.main), in worker and combined mode. Malformed, negative or non-finite values are ignored with a warning. ATLAN_POST_DRAIN_EXIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 120, or derived from ATLAN_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS Upper bound (seconds) on shutdown after the worker has drained on a shutdown signal. It is armed as soon as the Temporal drain returns, so it also covers the worker's own cleanup: credential directories, sizing rows, and the Pushgateway final push, hold and DELETE. It also covers closing infrastructure, flushing telemetry and interpreter exit hooks. No activity is in flight by then; if these steps have not finished within the bound the process exits with code 3, so a stuck telemetry flush cannot hold the pod for its whole grace period. The container entrypoint passes code 3 through as the container's exit code. Applies when the app is started through the SDK's entry point (python -m application_sdk.main); awaiting run_worker_mode / run_combined_mode directly does not start it unless bound_post_drain_exit=True. 0 or negative disables the bound. DAPR_STOP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 30 Read by the container entrypoint. How long to wait for daprd to exit once the Python app has exited before killing it. Once the app has exited, daprd has nothing left to do: inbound pub/sub and bindings have no app to deliver to, and the app has no outbound call in flight. ATLAN_TEMPORAL_CORE_METRICS_MAX_BYTES 1048576 Upper bound (bytes) on every read of Temporal core's loopback metrics endpoint: the poll-state diagnostic, the combined-mode /metrics proxy and the worker's Pushgateway TemporalCoreCollector. Guards each reader against an unbounded allocation if the local exporter misbehaves or grows high-cardinality. An oversize payload is skipped: the diagnostic reports unknown (never zero), /metrics is served without Temporal core series and counts temporal_core_metrics_proxy_failures_total{reason="oversize"}, and the collector skips that push. ATLAN_WORKER_EVICTION_MAX_RETRIES 3 Maximum re-dispatches of one activity caused by worker pod eviction (SIGTERM during the activity: scale-down, spot reclaim, node drain, rolling deploy). These do not consume the activity's retry-policy attempts. Negative values clamp to 0. ATLAN_WORKER_LIVENESS_MAX_IDLE_SECONDS 0 (off) When positive, the worker /live probe fails if no activity execution or heartbeat was recorded within this window. Enable it only for queues that are always busy: on an idle queue it restarts a healthy worker. ATLAN_DIRTY_RESTART_IDLE_MAX_SECONDS 150 Longest a restarted worker container idles before polling, when the restart advice says to wait, so a pod killed for memory can be replaced instead of taking work back on the same limit. It resumes polling either way. ATLAN_OOM_RESTART_CHECK none Whether a restarted worker container asks the activity rerouter what the restart earns before it polls again. api sends one GET to ATLAN_RESTART_ADVICE_URL naming this pod, and the worker waits only when the answer says a replacement is scheduled. none never asks and resumes polling at once. ATLAN_RESTART_ADVICE_URL (empty) Endpoint of the activity rerouter that a restarted worker asks whether it was killed and whether a replacement pod is coming. Used when ATLAN_OOM_RESTART_CHECK=api. Empty, no pod name, a timeout or an unparsable answer means the worker starts polling at once. K8S_POD_NAME (empty) Pod name, injected by the Kubernetes Downward API. Used to name this pod in restart advice, sizing telemetry and OTel resource attributes. Falls back to HOSTNAME. See Kubernetes-injected variables.

Reading the poller gauge requires Temporal core's Prometheus exporter, bound by ATLAN_TEMPORAL_PROMETHEUS_BIND_ADDRESS (default 127.0.0.1:9464). When it is unavailable the poll state is reported as unknown, never as zero.

docs.title: TLS
docs.text: Variable Default Description ATLAN_TEMPORAL_TLS_ENABLED false Enable mTLS for the Temporal connection. ATLAN_TEMPORAL_TLS_CA_CERT_PATH (empty) Path to the CA certificate file. ATLAN_TEMPORAL_TLS_CLIENT_CERT_PATH (empty) Path to the client certificate file. ATLAN_TEMPORAL_TLS_CLIENT_KEY_PATH (empty) Path to the client private key file. ATLAN_TEMPORAL_TLS_DOMAIN (empty) TLS server name override. ATLAN_WORKFLOW_TLS_ENABLED false v2-compat name for ATLAN_TEMPORAL_TLS_ENABLED. Read only when ATLAN_TEMPORAL_TLS_ENABLED is absent from the environment, so an explicit ATLAN_TEMPORAL_TLS_ENABLED=false wins over a stale value.

docs.title: HTTP Handler
docs.text: Variable Default Description ATLAN_HANDLER_HOST 0.0.0.0 Bind address for the FastAPI handler. Fallback: ATLAN_APP_HTTP_HOST. ATLAN_HANDLER_PORT 8000 HTTP port for the handler. Fallback: ATLAN_APP_HTTP_PORT. ATLAN_HEALTH_PORT 8081 Port for the worker health endpoint. ATLAN_HANDLER_MODULE (empty) Handler class to load (module:ClassName). Auto-discovered from the app module when unset. ATLAN_HANDLER_MAX_BODY_BYTES 4194304 (4 MiB) Largest request body the handler accepts on a route that reads its body whole: every route without a File or Form parameter, an app's own routes included. A larger body gets 413, whether it declares its Content-Length or not; it is counted as it arrives and never read whole. Applies to the worker's handler and to the consolidated API host. A non-integer or a value below 1 is ignored with a warning. ATLAN_HANDLER_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES 536870912 (512 MiB) Largest body accepted on a form route: /workflows/v1/file, or any route of the app's own (Handler.routers()) that declares a File or Form parameter, which is all an app does to take large uploads. The route decides, not the request's Content-Type. The upload is refused with 413 as soon as it passes the cap, before more of it is written to the pod's disk, and nothing is stored. Same parsing rules as ATLAN_HANDLER_MAX_BODY_BYTES. To accept a larger file (e.g. a multi-GB CSV), raise this on the pod that serves the route, e.g. 5368709120 for 5 GiB. There is no upper bound. The value is read once at startup, so restart the pod after changing it. It is per pod: on the consolidated API host it applies to every app that host serves. The upload is spooled to the pod's temp disk in full before it is stored, so give the pod ephemeral storage for the largest file times the concurrent uploads. Any body-size limit on the ingress in front of the pod still applies. ATLAN_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_DELAY_SECONDS 5 Event-loop yield (seconds) before tearing down the worker transport, giving in-flight activity completion RPCs a chance to flush. Distinct from TEMPORAL_GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT. TEMPORAL_GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT 3600, or derived from ATLAN_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS Seconds the Temporal worker waits for in-flight activities to finish on shutdown before cancelling them. TEMPORAL_MAX_CONCURRENT_ACTIVITIES derived from the container's limits Activity slots per worker. Unset or blank, the SDK derives it as min(100, 32 × CPUs, memory limit ÷ 64 MiB), never below 16. CPUs are the whole CPUs the process may use: the tighter of its CPU affinity and the CFS quota (a fractional quota rounds down, never below 1). Without a quota it is the affinity count, or the node's count where there is no affinity API. The memory limit is the cgroup's, falling back to K8S_POD_MEMORY_LIMIT; with neither, only the CPU term applies. A half-CPU pod under 1 GiB gets 16 slots, a 1-CPU, 2 GiB pod gets 32, and a pod with no known memory limit and at least 4 usable CPUs gets 100. The worker derives this once at startup and logs the value and its inputs (a value passed to create_worker(max_concurrent_activities=...) wins and is logged as such), and publishes the value it runs with as the temporal_worker_activity_slots_limit gauge. Set this to use an exact number instead.

docs.title: Blocking offload (run_in_thread)
docs.text: Variable Default Description ATLAN_OFFLOAD_MAX_THREADS_PER_APP (unset: no cap) Process-wide: set it in the deployment environment of the process that runs the apps (on the consolidated API host, the host's own deployment), not as an ATLAN_APPENV__<APP>__... setting. One value applies to every app in the process; there is no per-app override. Most run_in_thread calls each app may have in flight (running or queued). A call past it fails at once with a retryable ResourceExhaustedError (resource="offload_threads") instead of queueing. A call counts until its thread finishes, not until its caller stops waiting. On the consolidated API host, keep it at or below the app's blocking_threads pool width. A value that isn't a positive integer is ignored, with one warning. See ADR-0010.

docs.title: Authentication (Temporal)
docs.text:
Set these when ATLAN_AUTH_ENABLED=true to authenticate the worker and handler against a secured Temporal cluster.

Variable Default Description ATLAN_AUTH_ENABLED false Enable OAuth2 authentication for Temporal and for lifecycle events. One reader decides both, so a value such as 1 enables both or neither. ATLAN_AUTH_TOKEN_URL (empty) OAuth2 token endpoint. v2-compat fallback: ATLAN_AUTH_URL. ATLAN_AUTH_BASE_URL (empty) OAuth2 authorization base URL. v2-compat fallback: ATLAN_AUTH_URL. ATLAN_AUTH_CLIENT_ID (empty) OAuth2 client ID (direct env var). ATLAN_AUTH_CLIENT_SECRET (empty) OAuth2 client secret (direct env var). ATLAN_AUTH_SCOPES (empty) Space-separated OAuth2 scopes. ATLAN_DEPLOYMENT_SECRET_PATH ATLAN_DEPLOYMENT_SECRETS Key name in the deployment secret store that holds the auth credentials. ATLAN_AUTH_CLIENT_ID_KEY ATLAN_AUTH_CLIENT_ID Key name for the client ID within the deployment secret. ATLAN_AUTH_CLIENT_SECRET_KEY ATLAN_AUTH_CLIENT_SECRET Key name for the client secret within the deployment secret. ATLAN_INTERNAL_HERACLES_URL (empty) Deprecated, removed in v4.0.0. In-cluster base URL used by the deprecated AtlanOAuthClient.effective_token_url() (as <url>/oauth/token). No SDK path exchanges a token against it.

When ATLAN_AUTH_ENABLED is on, lifecycle events read the client credentials for their bearer token once and reuse them. If the credentials are missing or the token endpoint refuses them (a 4xx other than 408/429, or no access_token), events go out without auth and the lookup is not repeated for 60 s. If the secret store does not answer (not ready yet, throttled), the lookup is repeated after 5 s. A refusal discards the cached credentials, so a rotated credential is picked up within 60 s, without a restart. A transient exchange failure (5xx, 408/429, timeout) keeps the credentials, and the next event retries the exchange.

docs.title: Dapr Component Names
docs.text:
Dapr component names are read at module-import time (not at runtime) because the observability stack initialises before AppConfig exists.

Variable Default Description STATE_STORE_NAME statestore Dapr state store component name. SECRET_STORE_NAME secretstore Dapr secret store component name. DEPLOYMENT_OBJECT_STORE_NAME objectstore Dapr object store for workflow outputs and artifacts. Required — see The deployment object store is required. UPSTREAM_OBJECT_STORE_NAME atlan-objectstore Dapr object store for uploading data to the Atlan platform (SDR deployments only). If the named component is absent, upstream_storage is None and App.upload()/App.download() fall back to the deployment store. If the name equals DEPLOYMENT_OBJECT_STORE_NAME (in-cluster charts point both at one component), upstream_storage is the deployment store itself — one write, no self-copy — and ENABLE_ATLAN_UPLOAD logs a WARNING because there is no boundary to hand off across. Ask context.single_store, not upstream_storage is None, for the topology. See ADR-0014. EVENT_STORE_NAME eventstore Dapr pub/sub component name. ATLAN_EVENT_INGRESS_DIRECT_FALLBACK true When the Dapr EVENT_STORE_NAME binding fails in a way that proves the event got no response (connection, TLS or DNS failure, missing binding), publish the lifecycle event (worker_start, token_refresh, workflow/activity start/end) directly to Event Ingress over HTTPS from the app process, reusing the same payload and bearer token and the url of the bindings.http component on disk. Errors that may already have been delivered (an upstream HTTP status) are not re-sent over direct HTTPS; the publish_event activity's Temporal retry re-sends workflow_start / workflow_end through Dapr, so those two are at-least-once. activity_start / activity_end and worker_start / token_refresh are published inline and not retried: after such an error they are logged and dropped, so they are at-most-once. Every event carries metadata.event_id, the same on every retry of one workflow event, so consumers can dedupe. Backs off 60 s after a failed direct publish. Logged at WARNING as FALLBACK ACTIVE / Published event via direct HTTPS fallback, FALLBACK SKIPPED / FALLBACK SUSPENDED when not attempted, FALLBACK FAILED / FALLBACK UNAVAILABLE at ERROR. Set false to disable. DEPLOYMENT_SECRET_STORE_NAME deployment-secret-store Dapr secret store holding deployment-scoped secrets (auth credentials, etc.). DAPR_MAX_GRPC_MESSAGE_LENGTH 104857600 (100 MB) Maximum gRPC message size in bytes for Dapr client calls. Increase for apps that move large payloads through Dapr state or bindings. ATLAN_ENABLE_OBJECTSTORE (unset) Whether the chart deployed the deployment object store, derived from deploy.dapr.objectstore. Only explains the startup error when the store is missing: the store is required whatever this says. See The deployment object store is required. ATLAN_ENABLE_STATESTORE (unset) Whether the chart deployed the state store, derived from deploy.dapr.statestore in atlan.yaml. Startup compares it with the components the sidecar registered and logs any mismatch. It does not switch anything on or off. ATLAN_ENABLE_SECRETSTORE (unset) As ATLAN_ENABLE_STATESTORE, for the secret store (deploy.dapr.secretstore). ATLAN_ENABLE_EVENTSTORE (unset) As ATLAN_ENABLE_STATESTORE, for the event binding (deploy.dapr.eventstore). DAPR_HTTP_PORT (set by the sidecar) Dapr sidecar HTTP port, injected by Dapr. Its presence selects Dapr-backed infrastructure; without it the SDK reports no sidecar. The local dev runner (application_sdk.dev) sets it for its embedded sidecar. DAPR_GRPC_PORT (set by the sidecar) Dapr sidecar gRPC port. The local dev runner sets it for its embedded sidecar and restores the previous value afterwards. DAPR_COMPONENTS_PATH ./components Directory of the Dapr component YAMLs. The SDK reads the files there to resolve the observability object store and the event binding's URL. The local dev runner points it at its generated components. DAPR_LOG_LEVEL info daprd --log-level, set by the image entrypoint. In SDR mode the Dapr log forwarder, which relays daprd's logs into the SDK pipeline, also reads it to set the level it forwards at.

docs.title: The deployment object store is required
docs.text:
Every app reads and writes artifacts, credential files and observability exports through the deployment object store, so worker, handler and combined startup build it unconditionally. When no Dapr component named DEPLOYMENT_OBJECT_STORE_NAME exists in DAPR_COMPONENTS_PATH, startup logs an ERROR and fails with DeploymentObjectStoreMissingError (a StorageBindingNotFoundError, so existing except StorageBindingNotFoundError: / except StorageConfigError: handlers still catch it; audience APP_OWNER). The component-diagnostics pass at startup also logs the missing object store at ERROR, never as "disabled by config (expected)".

The usual cause is the app's contract: the atlan-app chart omits the component when atlan.yaml carries deploy.dapr.objectstore: false. Set it to true (dapr { objectstore = true } in contract/app.pkl), regenerate and redeploy. contract-toolkit defaults it to true, and conformance rule K029 flags a contract or atlan.yaml that sets it to false.

The error does not depend on ATLAN_ENABLE_OBJECTSTORE: the chart sets that variable on the env-seeder init container, not the app container, so the app usually sees it unset. When it is visible and false, the error message says so.

docs.title: Which Dapr components a deployed app gets
docs.text:
The Local Marketplace deployer turns the deploy.dapr block of atlan.yaml into the atlan-app chart's dapr.components.<name>.enabled values. It fills each component the block leaves out (or the whole block, when there is none) with its own default: true for objectstore and secretstore, false for the rest. A value the block states always wins, including false. The chart's own values have every component off, so these deployer defaults are what an app without a dapr block runs with.

Once a contract has a deploy block, contract-toolkit renders every component whenever at least one resolves to true (or customComponents is non-empty), so the contract decides each one. When every component resolves to false (for example objectstore = false on an app without credentials), the toolkit emits no dapr block at all, and the deployer's defaults above apply instead. secretstore defaults to true for an app that resolves credentials (hasCredentialConfig or additionalCredentialConfigs, on the app or any entrypoint): the SDK resolves every credential through it, and without it each lookup fails with HTTP 500 from /v1.0/secrets/<store>/<guid>. Conformance rule K030 flags secretstore: false on such an app.

docs.title: Dapr Sidecar Readiness / Cold-Start Retry
docs.text:
Variable Default Description ATLAN_DAPR_SIDECAR_WAIT_TIMEOUT 60 Max seconds to poll /v1.0/healthz at startup for daprd to start accepting connections. Startup proceeds as soon as daprd answers the probe at all (per-component readiness is covered by each call site's cold-start retry budget); only connection errors poll to this deadline. Increase for pathologically slow cold starts (image pull + daprd boot). ATLAN_DAPR_COLD_START_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS 120.0 Seconds a Dapr-backed call (secret fetch, credential-vault config fetch, ...) may retry a cold-sidecar race before giving up. Shared by every call site that opts into retry_past_dapr_cold_start. Env-overridable for pathologically slow runners.

Within each attempt of that budget, the Dapr HTTP client replays a failed GET up to 3 times (2-12 s of backoff) on a connection error or HTTP 500/502/503/504. One answer is not replayed: a secret GET that Dapr answers with HTTP 500 ERR_SECRET_GET and a "not found" message (including Kubernetes' invalid-name rejection) fails after one request, since the answer won't change. Every other 500, such as a throttled secret store, is still replayed.

docs.title: Redis (deprecated, removed in v4.0.0)
docs.text:
These configure only the deprecated RedisClient / RedisClientAsync, which keep working until v4.0.0. The SDK's distributed lock is not wired in v3: create_worker registers no lock interceptor, so needs_lock has no effect whatever these are set to. These variables do not configure a capacity pool either: RedisCapacityPool is deprecated and the framework never constructed one. Leave them empty unless your app uses the deprecated clients.

Variable Default Description REDIS_HOST (empty) Redis host for direct connection. Leave empty to use Sentinel. REDIS_PORT (empty) Redis port for direct connection. REDIS_PASSWORD (empty) Redis password. REDIS_SENTINEL_SERVICE_NAME mymaster Redis Sentinel service name. REDIS_SENTINEL_HOSTS (empty) Comma-separated host:port pairs for Redis Sentinel. IS_LOCKING_DISABLED true The Redis clients' connect guard: while true, RedisClient / RedisClientAsync do not connect and leave redis_client as None. Set to false to let them connect. It does not turn on distributed locking, which v3 does not wire. LOCK_RETRY_INTERVAL_SECONDS 60 Read only by the lock interceptor, which create_worker never registers. Has no effect.

docs.title: MCP
docs.text: Variable Default Description ENABLE_MCP false Start an MCP server alongside the handler. Requires the mcp extra: uv add "atlan-application-sdk[mcp]".

docs.title: SQL Client
docs.text: Variable Default Description ATLAN_SQL_USE_SERVER_SIDE_CURSOR true Use server-side cursors for SQL queries. Reduces memory for large result sets by streaming data row-by-row. Default: enabled. To disable, set the variable to a false word (e.g. ATLAN_SQL_USE_SERVER_SIDE_CURSOR=false) or to an empty value. An unrecognised word warns and keeps cursors enabled.

docs.title: DuckDB (incremental extraction, query transformer)
docs.text: Variable Default Description ATLAN_DUCKDB_MEMORY_LIMIT (derived) Memory limit for a DuckDBConnectionManager opened without an explicit memory_limit, as a DuckDB size string (e.g. 1GB, 768MiB). When unset it is half of the container's free memory (limit minus current usage) at open time, split evenly with the other DuckDB connections open in the process, between 256 MiB and 2 GB; 2 GB when no container limit is known. Above the limit DuckDB spills to its temp directory, which lowers the risk of growing the worker into an OOM kill.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text: Variable Default Description ATLAN_MAX_CONCURRENT_STORAGE_TRANSFERS 4 Maximum concurrent object-store uploads/downloads. ATLAN_OBSTORE_READ_TIMEOUT 90s Progress-based liveness bound: a transfer fails only if no bytes arrive for this long (the timer resets on every successful read). The primary timeout — a slow-but-progressing transfer survives; a genuine stall fails fast. ATLAN_OBSTORE_TIMEOUT 30m Overall-request wall-clock backstop per object-store request. Scales with file size, not throughput, so it is deliberately generous; ATLAN_OBSTORE_READ_TIMEOUT is the real liveness bound. A value that is not a duration (see How values are read) warns and keeps the default, as do the other ATLAN_OBSTORE_*_TIMEOUT variables. ATLAN_OBSTORE_CONNECT_TIMEOUT 30s Object-store client connect timeout (duration). ATLAN_OBSTORE_POOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT 90s How long an idle pooled connection is kept (duration). ATLAN_OBSTORE_HTTP2_KEEP_ALIVE_TIMEOUT 30s HTTP/2 keep-alive ping timeout (duration). ATLAN_OBSTORE_POOL_MAX_IDLE_PER_HOST (client default) Maximum idle pooled connections per host. Unset keeps the object-store client's default. ATLAN_OBSTORE_USER_AGENT atlan-application-sdk/<version> User-Agent sent on object-store requests. ATLAN_OBSTORE_RETRY_MAX_RETRIES obstore default (10) Maximum retries the object-store client (obstore's Rust layer) makes for a failed request, with backoff. The SDK adds no Python-level retry on top. A malformed or negative value logs a warning and keeps the default. ATLAN_OBSTORE_RETRY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS obstore default (180) Integer seconds the object-store client keeps retrying a failed request before giving up. A malformed or negative value logs a warning and keeps the default. ATLAN_STORAGE_RESUME_DOWNLOADS true Kill-switch for resumable chunked downloads. When enabled, an interrupted chunked download keeps its in-flight part file and checkpoint sidecar (.sdk-partial/{name}.part and .sdk-partial/{name}.transfer-state beside the destination), and a retry fetches only the missing ranges. Set to false to restore delete-partial-on-failure behaviour. ATLAN_STORAGE_PROGRESS_LOG_INTERVAL_SECONDS 30 Interval (seconds) between in-progress heartbeat log lines during a long upload/download. 0 disables heartbeats. ATLAN_STORAGE_LOCK_WAIT_PROGRESS_SECONDS 30 Interval (seconds) between progress marks while an activity waits on a per-destination storage lock (a second download of the same path queues behind the first). Capped at a quarter of ATLAN_MAX_NO_PROGRESS_SECONDS so a queued activity is never killed as stalled; floored at 1. ATLAN_STORAGE_VERIFY_TRANSFERS true Kill-switch for transfer integrity validation. When enabled, every upload confirms the local file did not shrink while it was read and that the store recorded the bytes that were sent, and every download confirms it wrote as many bytes as the store declared and — when a {key}.sha256 sidecar exists — that they hash to the digest the producer recorded. A content mismatch raises the non-retryable StorageIntegrityError. Set to false for a backend whose HEAD-after-write is not read-your-writes consistent. ATLAN_STORAGE_WRITE_SIDECARS true Kill-switch for {key}.sha256 sidecar emission. Sidecars are what let a downstream app detect an artifact its producer truncated. Set to false for a deployment whose object-store consumers cannot tolerate the extra keys (e.g. a reader that globs a prefix without filtering sidecars). Verification is independent — downloads still verify whatever sidecars they find. The consolidated API host's file upload route honours it too. ATLAN_STORE_ASSERT_ENABLED false Opt-in for the e2e sdk:store-assert node, which checks what an app left in the object store. The workflow is registered on every worker either way; unset, the node reads nothing and reports itself disabled. Set only on e2e tenants, by the e2e install through deploy.env_overrides. Never set it on a customer tenant. ATLAN_FILE_REF_CHUNKED_THRESHOLD_BYTES 33554432 (32 MiB) FileReference size threshold above which downloads use parallel range GETs. ATLAN_FILE_REF_CHUNK_SIZE_BYTES 16777216 (16 MiB) Size of each range-GET chunk in a chunked download. ATLAN_FILE_REF_CHUNK_CONCURRENCY 4 Maximum concurrent range-GET chunks per file. ATLAN_STORAGE_TRANSFER_MEMORY_BUDGET_BYTES 0 (derived) Bytes of transfer buffers the SDK's file transfers in the process may hold at once — the range GETs, streaming downloads and multipart uploads behind download_file, upload_file, the prefix operations and FileReference hand-offs reserve from one budget, so the per-call concurrency limits cannot multiply past it. upload_bytes and every CloudStore transfer reserve like any other; put_json and CloudStore.get_bytes() hold each object in memory outside the budget. 0 takes a quarter of the container memory limit (never under 128 MiB; 1 GiB when no limit is known). A transfer queued on the budget marks progress, so it is never killed as stalled. ATLAN_STORAGE_UPLOAD_PART_SIZE_BYTES 8388608 (8 MiB) Multipart upload part size. Larger parts mean fewer parts and a shorter completion window for large objects. Peak upload memory is roughly this times ATLAN_STORAGE_UPLOAD_MAX_CONCURRENCY. ATLAN_STORAGE_UPLOAD_MAX_CONCURRENCY 12 Parts uploaded concurrently per multipart upload. Lower it when raising the part size, to hold peak memory steady. ATLAN_UPLOAD_FILE_BLOCKED_PATHS (empty) Comma-separated substrings. A local path containing any of them is refused by the file-upload helpers, in addition to the built-in system, credential and .env* paths. \ and / are matched alike. ATLAN_SDR_PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SECS 30 Per-store timeout for the SDR boot-time object-store access probe (runs when ENABLE_ATLAN_UPLOAD=true). Non-finite or non-positive values use the default. ENABLE_ATLAN_UPLOAD false Enable uploading processed artifacts to the Atlan platform object store. ATLAN_DEPLOYMENT_ARTIFACT_DUAL_WRITE best_effort Controls dual-write behaviour when both stores are configured (SDR only). best_effort (default): artifact is written to the deployment (customer) store and the upstream (Atlan) store; a deployment-write failure logs a WARNING and the run continues. required: same dual-write, but a deployment-write failure causes the run to fail after the upstream write completes (a copy is guaranteed somewhere). disabled: upstream-only write (pre-BLDX-1464 behaviour). ATLAN_VALIDATE_ASSETS_ON_UPLOAD true Validate transformed assets against the pyatlan_v9 backbone before the SDR→Atlan upload handoff. Warn-only — invalid/orphaned assets are logged, never block the upload. Set to false to disable the check entirely. ATLAN_VALIDATE_ASSETS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 600 Upper bound in seconds for one upload's asset-validation scan. The scan runs in an isolated child process (CNCT-85); past this bound the child is killed and the upload proceeds with a warning, so warn-only validation can neither stall nor crash a handoff. ATLAN_VALIDATE_ARTIFACTS true Deployment-level kill switch for artifact validation. When on, an outcome event is emitted for every artifact. false stops validation and its events. Whether a verdict blocks is ATLAN_ARTIFACT_VALIDATION_MODE. ATLAN_ARTIFACT_VALIDATION_MODE (the app's artifact_validation_mode, else soft) hard makes a failed artifact validation block; any other non-empty value is soft. Overrides the app class's declaration. ATLAN_FAULT_ISOLATION_IDLE_SECONDS 30 Seconds a fault-isolation process pool (run_fault_isolated / run_best_effort, which the asset-validation scans use) keeps its spawn children after its last call finishes. Past it the children exit and their memory returns to the pod; the next call spawns afresh. 0 shuts the pool down as soon as it goes idle. Read when a pool goes idle, so a change applies from the next idle period. A value that isn't a non-negative number is ignored, with one warning. See ADR-0017. SSL_CERT_DIR (empty) Directory of custom CA certificates (.pem, .crt, .cer, .ca-bundle). Used by the SDK's httpx clients when set.

docs.title: Consolidated API host object store
docs.text:
The consolidated API host serves object-store routes for its hosted apps from one store, built from these variables. The host's manifest aliases them from the atlan-app chart's per-cloud values. The first bucket or account set wins, in this order: GCP, S3, Azure. With none set the routes answer 503.

Variable Default Description ATLAN_GCP_BUCKET (empty) GCS bucket, reached through its S3-compatible endpoint. Needs both HMAC keys below. ATLAN_GCP_REGION (empty) GCS region. ATLAN_GCP_HMAC_ACCESS_KEY (empty) GCS HMAC access key. ATLAN_GCP_HMAC_SECRET (empty) GCS HMAC secret. ATLAN_S3_BUCKET (empty) S3 bucket, using the pod's ambient AWS identity. ATLAN_S3_REGION AWS_REGION, then AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, then us-east-1 S3 region. ATLAN_AZURE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT (empty) Azure Blob storage account. Needs ATLAN_AZURE_STORAGE_CONTAINER. ATLAN_AZURE_STORAGE_CONTAINER (empty) Azure Blob container. ATLAN_AZURE_STORAGE_ACCESS_KEY (empty) Account key. Unset means the pod's ambient (workload) identity.

docs.title: Outbound proxy
docs.text:
Every SDK connection that can go through an egress proxy resolves it with one rule (application_sdk/_proxy.py): the BaseClient HTTP transport, the obstore object-store clients, the Temporal connection and the S3 bucket-region lookup.

  1. The proxy for a connection is its scheme's variable, then ALL_PROXY: HTTPS_PROXY for TLS connections (object stores, a TLS Temporal endpoint, https:// requests), HTTP_PROXY for plaintext ones. HTTP_PROXY is never used for a TLS connection.
  2. A host matching NO_PROXY connects directly: an exact host, a domain suffix (.example.com or example.com match subdomains), or * for every host. A port on the host is ignored. obstore receives the raw list as proxy_excludes and matches it per request itself.
  3. Only the process environment is read. The lowercase spelling (https_proxy) wins over the uppercase one. Operating-system proxy settings (macOS System Settings, the Windows registry) are ignored, so a laptop resolves the same way a pod does.
Variable Default Description HTTPS_PROXY (empty) Proxy URL (http://[user[:password]@]host:port) for TLS connections. HTTP_PROXY (empty) Proxy URL for plaintext connections. ALL_PROXY (empty) Proxy URL for any connection whose scheme variable is unset. NO_PROXY (empty) Comma-separated hosts and domain suffixes that connect directly.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: Variable Default Description ATLAN_LOG_LEVEL INFO Log level (DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR). Fallback: LOG_LEVEL. CRITICAL is accepted by loguru but prohibited in app code per ADR-0011. ATLAN_LOG_DIAGNOSE false Annotate console tracebacks with the values of the names on each frame's source line (loguru's diagnose). Off by default, unlike loguru's own default: those values print verbatim, so a credential dict passed to a failing call has its contents rendered onto stderr. Useful locally; leave off anywhere real credentials exist. Independent of ATLAN_LOG_LEVEL by design — raising verbosity to DEBUG does not re-enable it. Traceback frames are unaffected either way. ATLAN_LOG_BATCH_SIZE 100 Records buffered before flushing to the object-store sink. ATLAN_LOG_FLUSH_INTERVAL_SECONDS 10 Seconds between object-store sink flushes. ATLAN_OBSERVABILITY_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 10 Upper bound, in seconds, on stopping the observability background loop at process exit. Covers the final flush of every periodic sink (logs, metrics, traces, sizing) and the Segment sender's last batch together. Past it, the remaining work is abandoned. See Monitoring. ATLAN_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS (removed) No longer read; setting it logs a startup warning. The SDK never deletes exported files; bound object-store growth with a lifecycle rule on the bucket, for example expiring objects under artifacts/apps/observability/ after N days. See ADR-0012. ATLAN_LOG_CLEANUP_ENABLED (removed) No longer read; setting it logs a startup warning. See ATLAN_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS. ATLAN_LOG_FILE_NAME log.parquet Signal-type discriminator used internally to route records to the correct observability sub-path (logs / metrics / traces). The default is kept as log.parquet for back-compat; the on-disk and object-store format is gzip-compressed NDJSON (.json.gz), not parquet. ATLAN_LOG_SOURCE ATLAN_APPLICATION_NAME source label on log lines from the app's own code (not SDK or dependency lines, which are classified automatically). Services built on the SDK that are not connectors set their own, for example ae. ATLAN_LOG_CLOUDFLARE_504_SUMMARY_INTERVAL_SECONDS 60 Minimum seconds between repeated INFO summaries from the filter that suppresses Cloudflare 504s on Temporal long polls. ENABLE_WORKFLOW_REPLAY_LOGS false Emit SDK log lines during Temporal workflow replay. Off matches Temporal's own workflow.logger; turn on to debug with a Replayer.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text: Variable Default Description ATLAN_METRICS_BATCH_SIZE 100 Records buffered before flushing to the object-store sink. ATLAN_METRICS_FLUSH_INTERVAL_SECONDS 10 Seconds between object-store sink flushes. ATLAN_METRICS_FILE_NAME metrics.parquet Signal-type discriminator for metrics records, as ATLAN_LOG_FILE_NAME is for logs. Not a real file name. ATLAN_SIZING_BATCH_SIZE 500 Activity sizing-telemetry records buffered before a flush. ATLAN_SIZING_FLUSH_INTERVAL_SECONDS 60 Seconds between sizing-telemetry flushes. ATLAN_SIZING_FILE_NAME sizing.parquet Signal-type discriminator for sizing records. APPLICATION_SDK_ENABLE_SIZING_TELEMETRY false Collect per-activity peak memory and CPU throttling. APPLICATION_SDK_SIZING_TELEMETRY_ACTIVITIES (empty: none) Comma-separated activity names to measure, or * for all. Empty collects nothing (and logs a warning when sizing telemetry is on). APPLICATION_SDK_SIZING_TELEMETRY_POLL_SECONDS 1.0 Memory poll interval when the kernel watermark is unusable. 0 disables polling, so kernels before 6.8 collect no peak. ATLAN_METRICS_RETENTION_DAYS (removed) No longer read; setting it logs a startup warning. The SDK never deleted exported metric files. Use a bucket lifecycle rule, as for ATLAN_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS. ATLAN_METRICS_CLEANUP_ENABLED (removed) No longer read; setting it logs a startup warning. See ATLAN_METRICS_RETENTION_DAYS. ATLAN_ENABLE_TEMPORAL_CORE_METRICS true Bind the Temporal Rust-core Prometheus endpoint at ATLAN_TEMPORAL_PROMETHEUS_BIND_ADDRESS (loopback) in worker/combined mode so its metric set (temporal_workflow_*, temporal_activity_*, etc.) is reachable for the combined-mode FastAPI /metrics proxy and the worker's TemporalCoreCollector. The FastAPI /metrics route is always exposed regardless of this flag — when this flag is false, or in handler-only mode, the response simply omits the proxied Temporal Rust-core families. run_dev_combined() defaults to false to avoid hot-reload port collisions. See Monitoring. ATLAN_PROMETHEUS_PUSHGATEWAY_URL (empty) Pushgateway URL workers push to (split deployment). Empty disables push — combined-mode pods leave it unset and rely on direct /metrics scrape. ATLAN_PROMETHEUS_PUSHGATEWAY_INTERVAL_SECONDS 30 Periodic push interval. A final push always happens on shutdown. ATLAN_PROMETHEUS_PUSHGATEWAY_DELETE_ON_SHUTDOWN true DELETE the worker's group from the gateway on graceful shutdown so stopped pods don't leave sticky data. ATLAN_PROMETHEUS_PUSHGATEWAY_SWEEP_STALE_ON_START true On worker startup, sweep stale {job=mine, instance=other} groups left by predecessors that died ungracefully. ATLAN_PROMETHEUS_PUSHGATEWAY_SWEEP_STALENESS_SECONDS 300 Don't reap groups whose last push is more recent than this. Protects live siblings during rolling deploys. ATLAN_PROMETHEUS_PUSHGATEWAY_HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 10, or derived from ATLAN_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS Per-request HTTP timeout for every Pushgateway call. ATLAN_PROMETHEUS_PUSHGATEWAY_SHUTDOWN_DELETE_DELAY_SECONDS 35, or derived from ATLAN_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS Sleep between final push and DELETE on shutdown so Prometheus has at least one scrape window to read the final batch. ATLAN_TEMPORAL_CORE_METRICS_PROXY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 5.0 Per-request HTTP timeout (seconds) for the in-process FastAPI /metrics proxy fetching Temporal Rust-core series from ATLAN_TEMPORAL_PROMETHEUS_BIND_ADDRESS when the proxy is enabled. Increase if the loopback fetch times out under heavy load.

docs.title: Traces
docs.text: Variable Default Description ATLAN_ENABLE_OTLP_TRACES false Export traces via OTLP to OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT. run_main installs the process-wide tracer provider at startup, so worker spans from the Temporal TraceInterceptor are exported. ATLAN_ENABLE_TRACES_CONSOLE false Development only. Also print every span to stdout via OTel's ConsoleSpanExporter. Has no effect unless ATLAN_ENABLE_OTLP_TRACES is on. Leave off in deployed pods: it puts every span on the log stream. ATLAN_TRACES_FILE_NAME traces.parquet Signal-type discriminator for the traces adapter. No traces file is written: spans go over OTLP.

docs.title: OpenTelemetry
docs.text:
Variable Default Description ATLAN_SERVICE_NAME (empty) Runtime override for OTel service name. AppConfig reads this first; if set, it supersedes both OTEL_SERVICE_NAME and the name derived from the --app module. Import-time telemetry reads OTEL_SERVICE_NAME only — set both if you need consistent naming across all telemetry paths. OTEL_SERVICE_NAME atlan-application-sdk Service name in telemetry data. At runtime, AppConfig overrides this with ATLAN_SERVICE_NAME (if set) or a name derived from the --app module; import-time telemetry (traces/metrics adaptors) reads only OTEL_SERVICE_NAME directly. OTEL_SERVICE_VERSION (SDK version) Service version in telemetry data. OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES (empty) Additional OTel resource attributes (key=value pairs). OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT http://localhost:4317 OTLP collector endpoint. Set to the node IP collector in Kubernetes: $(K8S_NODE_IP):4317. ENABLE_OTLP_LOGS false Export logs via OTLP to OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT. ENABLE_OTLP_WORKFLOW_LOGS false Add a second OTLP log exporter for workflow-log archival. Needs OTEL_WORKFLOW_LOGS_ENDPOINT. OTEL_WORKFLOW_LOGS_ENDPOINT (empty) Endpoint of the secondary, archival OTLP log collector. OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN http Read by OTel instrumentation, once per process. The handler service sets it to http when unset, so HTTP metrics use the stable names (http_server_request_duration_seconds, in seconds). An explicit value replaces that default: keep http in it (or http/dup to emit both stable and legacy names), or the legacy http_server_duration_milliseconds comes back.

| OTEL_WF_NODE_NAME | (empty) | Kubernetes node name for workflow telemetry. | | OTEL_EXPORTER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS | 30 | Timeout for OTLP export operations. | | OTEL_BATCH_DELAY_MS | 5000 | Delay between batch exports (milliseconds). | | OTEL_BATCH_SIZE | 512 | Maximum export batch size. | | OTEL_QUEUE_SIZE | 2048 | Maximum export queue size. | | ATLAN_ENABLE_OBSERVABILITY_STORE_SINK | true | Write observability data to the object store sink. Fallback: ATLAN_ENABLE_OBSERVABILITY_DAPR_SINK. | | ATLAN_BASE_URL | (empty) | Atlan instance base URL. Used by the events interceptor. |

docs.title: Local development
docs.text:
Most defaults work out of the box for local development with uv run poe start-deps (starts Dapr + Temporal). The key variables to override:

ATLAN_APP_MODULE=app.app:MyExtractor
ATLAN_APPLICATION_NAME=my-extractor
ATLAN_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG

docs.title: ATLAN_LOCAL_DEVELOPMENT (app-level, not read by the SDK)
docs.text:
The SDK itself does not read ATLAN_LOCAL_DEVELOPMENT; it infers local development from the registered components. Many connector main.py files still read it, as a contract between the app and the SDK's CI: when it is true and DAPR_HTTP_PORT is unset, main.py calls app.run_dev, which boots an embedded daprd and an in-process Temporal. Otherwise it calls application_sdk.main.main(), which expects an external Dapr sidecar.

The shared connector-integration-tests action sets ATLAN_LOCAL_DEVELOPMENT: "true" on its "Start app server" and test steps, and on SDK 3.13+ it starts no external daprd or Temporal. Removing the variable from the action leaves those apps with no sidecar, and they fail at startup with DaprNotDetectedError. .github/scripts/tests/test_connector_integration_local_dev_env.py pins it. Because apps still read it, it is not in _REMOVED_ENV_VARS, and setting it does not trigger the removed-variable warning.

docs.title: Production deployment
docs.text:
ATLAN_APP_MODULE=app.app:MyExtractor          # required
ATLAN_TEMPORAL_HOST=temporal.internal:7233    # production Temporal cluster
ATLAN_TEMPORAL_NAMESPACE=my-namespace
ATLAN_AUTH_ENABLED=true
ATLAN_AUTH_TOKEN_URL=https://auth.internal/oauth2/token
ATLAN_AUTH_CLIENT_ID=…                        # or use deployment secret store
ATLAN_AUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=…
ENABLE_ATLAN_UPLOAD=true
ATLAN_ENABLE_TEMPORAL_CORE_METRICS=true       # default; binds Temporal Rust-core on 127.0.0.1:9464 (loopback) for combined /metrics proxy and worker pushes
# /metrics is always exposed on the FastAPI handler port (default 8000) — no env-var gate
# For worker-only pods (split deployment), set the Pushgateway URL instead:
# ATLAN_PROMETHEUS_PUSHGATEWAY_URL=http://prometheus-pushgateway.monitoring.svc.cluster.local:9091

ATLAN_MAX_CONCURRENT_STORAGE_TRANSFERS=8      # higher on fast network
DAPR_MAX_GRPC_MESSAGE_LENGTH=209715200        # 200 MB for large payloads

docs.title: RCA: Temporal Worker Shutdown Deadlock — Phantom Task Slot
docs.text: Date: 2026-03-27 Component: application-sdk (AppWorker.__aexit__) Impact: Worker pod stuck in Terminating state for 12 hours, blocking workflow processing Fix: Add event-loop yield in AppWorker.__aexit__ before delegating to Worker.__aexit__

docs.title: Incident Summary
docs.text: An automation-engine worker pod remained in Terminating state for 12 hours after receiving SIGTERM. During this time, the Temporal worker held a phantom "in-use" task slot that could never be released, blocking worker.shutdown() from completing until the graceful_shutdown_timeout (12 hours) expired. Other workflows queued behind this worker experienced delays of up to 39 minutes.

docs.title: Root Cause
docs.text: A race condition between SIGTERM signal handling and the Temporal SDK's activity completion flow.

docs.title: What happened
docs.text:
1. The worker received an activity (save_workflow_run_state, attempt 2)
  2. The activity failed — Atlas API rejected the payload (appWorkflowRunDag exceeds limit of 100000 characters)
  3. 3 seconds later, SIGTERM arrived (deployment rollout)
  4. The Temporal Python SDK's Worker.run() handles SIGTERM internally: it signals its internal task to stop, causing worker.run() to return
  5. The async with AppWorker(...): context manager exited, invoking AppWorker.__aexit__
  6. AppWorker.__aexit__ immediately delegated to Worker.__aexit__, which called shutdown() — stopping all pollers and waiting for in-flight task slots to drain

docs.title: Why it deadlocked
docs.text:
The Temporal Python SDK processes activity completions in an async coroutine (_run_activity in temporalio/worker/_activity.py). After an activity function raises an exception, _run_activity must:

  1. Encode the failure into a completion protobuf (line 360)
  2. Await the last heartbeat task (line 383)
  3. Call await self._bridge_worker().complete_activity_task(completion) (line 392) — this sends RespondActivityTaskFailed to the Temporal server
  4. Remove the activity from _running_activities (line 393) — this frees the task slot

When Worker.run() returned due to SIGTERM, AppWorker.__aexit__ was called immediately — with no await before delegating to Worker.__aexit__. This meant worker.shutdown() ran without yielding the event loop, changing the Temporal SDK's internal state before _run_activity could reach complete_activity_task().

docs.title: Evidence from production metrics
docs.text:
Metrics from the stuck worker pod (automation-engine-worker-8696997456-z2rwj):

temporal_num_pollers{activity_task}:        0    (stopped by shutdown)
temporal_num_pollers{sticky_workflow_task}:  0    (stopped by shutdown)
temporal_worker_task_slots_used{ActivityWorker}:  1    (phantom — never freed)
temporal_worker_task_slots_used{WorkflowWorker}:  1    (phantom — never freed)
temporal_sticky_cache_size:                       1    (workflow stuck in cache)
temporal_request{RespondActivityTaskFailed}:       (absent — never sent)
temporal_request{RespondWorkflowTaskCompleted}:    (absent — never sent)

The worker had zero pollers (shutdown stopped them) but still held 1 activity + 1 workflow slot as "in-use". Zero Respond* RPCs were ever made — confirming the activity completion was preempted.

docs.title: Timeline
docs.text: Time (UTC) Event 11:14:53 Worker pod z2rwj starts 11:15:05 Activity save_workflow_run_state (attempt 2) received and executed — Atlas error 11:15:08 SIGTERM received — Temporal SDK signals worker.run() to stop 11:15:08 worker.run() returns → AppWorker.__aexit__ → Worker.__aexit__ → worker.shutdown() called — pollers stopped, waiting for in-flight slots 11:15:08+ _run_activity never reaches complete_activity_task() — slot never freed 12:46:26 Temporal server-side terminates the workflow (heartbeat timeout) 12:46:26+ Worker never learns about termination (pollers stopped) ~23:15 graceful_shutdown_timeout (12h) would expire — pod finally exits

docs.title: Fix
docs.text: Add an asyncio.sleep(SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_DELAY_SECONDS) in AppWorker.__aexit__ before delegating to Worker.__aexit__. This yields the event loop, allowing any pending _run_activity coroutines to reach complete_activity_task() and flush their RPCs before shutdown changes the SDK state.

docs.title: Why asyncio.sleep is correct here
docs.text:
The sleep doesn't need to wait for the gRPC call (complete_activity_task) to finish — that's what graceful_shutdown_timeout handles. It only needs to let _run_activity get scheduled on the event loop to reach the complete_activity_task() call. This is a microseconds operation; the 5-second default is massively overprovisioned.

Once complete_activity_task() is called, the Rust core knows about the completion. worker.shutdown() will then properly wait for the gRPC response and release the task slot, all within the existing graceful_shutdown_timeout.

docs.title: Changes
docs.text:
application_sdk/constants.py - Added SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_DELAY_SECONDS (default: 5, configurable via ATLAN_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_DELAY_SECONDS)

application_sdk/execution/_temporal/worker.py - AppWorker.__aexit__(): added await asyncio.sleep(SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_DELAY_SECONDS) before delegating to self._worker.__aexit__()

tests/unit/execution/test_worker.py - TestShutdownDrainDelay: 4 new tests that reproduce the race condition and prove the fix: - test_without_drain_delay_activity_completion_preempted — with delay=0 (old code), the activity completion never runs. Reproduces the bug. - test_with_drain_delay_activity_completes_before_shutdown — with delay>0 (new code), the activity completion runs first. Proves the fix. - test_drain_delay_flushes_multiple_pending_completions — multiple pending completions all flush - test_aexit_completes_even_with_zero_delay — no regression when no in-flight work

docs.title: Contributing Factors
docs.text:
These are separate issues that amplified the impact but are not addressed in this PR:

  1. KEDA ScaledObject paused (autoscaling.keda.sh/paused: "true") — manually annotated since March 19, preventing autoscaling. Single worker had to process all workflows serially.

  2. Atlas appWorkflowRunDag 100K character limit — the activity that triggered the race fails deterministically for large DAGs. All 3 retry attempts fail with the same error.

  3. terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 43230 (12 hours) — matches graceful_shutdown_timeout but means the pod lingers in Terminating state for the full duration of the deadlock. (Later note, FND-4645: the SDK's own drain default is 3600 s, not 12 h. The two only agree when a deployment sets TEMPORAL_GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT explicitly, or declares its grace through ATLAN_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS so the drain is derived from it.)

docs.title: Upgrade Guide: v2 → v3
docs.text:
Application SDK v3.0 introduces three major improvements:

  1. Schema-driven contracts — typed Input/Output Pydantic models replace Dict[str, Any]
  2. Infrastructure abstraction — Protocol-based interfaces decouple services from Dapr
  3. Temporal abstraction — App + @task replace @workflow.defn + @activity.defn

Current version: 3.5.0. This guide covers the v2 → v3.0 migration steps. For additions since v3.0, see the callout below.

Added since v3.0 (highlights for connectors upgrading incrementally):

  • v3.1 — [sql] extra split; [azure] and [distributed_lock] extras lazy-loaded so importing core symbols (App, BaseSQLClient) never pulls optional deps.
  • v3.2 — OAuthTokenService promoted to public API (from application_sdk.credentials import OAuthTokenService).
  • v3.4 — get_logger and AtlanLoggerAdapter (including .opt()) exposed as top-level public API (from application_sdk.observability import get_logger).
  • v3.5 — mcp_tool / MCPServer lazy-loaded; clients/__init__ lazy-loads AzureClient, RedisClient, RedisClientAsync.

v3.0 is a clean break from v2. All v2 Python module paths raise ImportError — update all imports to their v3 equivalents using the quick reference below. A set of environment-variable aliases remain to ease the infrastructure rollout (e.g. Helm charts that still set ATLAN_WORKFLOW_HOST or APPLICATION_MODE) — see Configuration for the full alias list. One legacy helper, application_sdk.common.error_codes, is retained for back-compat; prefer application_sdk.errors for new code.

Shipping an app? Run through standards/v3-readiness.md before declaring the upgrade complete — it's the sign-off checklist for app owners and reviewers.
